title: Selection proof: Even-key census
topics: Greedy choices, dynamic programming and backtracking
summary: Choose any subset of reading positions, including the empty subset, and sum its readings. Produce every distinct achievable sum in ascending order. Equal readings at different positions remain separate choices. Return how many values in the derived sequence are even, including 0 and negative even values.
descriptionMd:
A sample tray allows each physical slip to be either included or excluded from a signed total. Alma separates readings for the office's even-numbered keys. A zero reading belongs in that count, just like any other even number.

Choose any subset of reading positions, including the empty subset, and sum its readings. Produce every distinct achievable sum in ascending order. Equal readings at different positions remain separate choices.

Return how many values in the derived sequence are even, including 0 and negative even values.

Implement selectionProofEvenKeyCensus(readings, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.
unitIntro: Backtracking choices. Choose any subset of reading positions, including the empty subset, and sum its readings. Produce every distinct achievable sum in ascending order. Equal readings at different positions remain separate choices. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys.
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.
Numeric readings lie between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000, subject to the task's shape and ordering rules.

Target time O(n*2^n); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(2^n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
hints: Start with backtracking choices. What state describes the portion you have already processed?

Choose any subset of reading positions, including the empty subset, and sum its readings. Produce every distinct achievable sum in ascending order. Equal readings at different positions remain separate choices. Derive each required reading once; do not restart the whole procedure for every output position.
Return how many values in the derived sequence are even, including 0 and negative even values. Handle the empty derived sequence according to the stated return rule.

cases.explanation: The derived sequence is [-3,0,4,7,9,11,12,14,16,19,23,26]. Return how many values in the derived sequence are even, including 0 and negative even values. This gives 6.
The derived sequence is [-2,0,2,4,6,8,10,12]. Return how many values in the derived sequence are even, including 0 and negative even values. This gives 8.
The derived sequence is [0]. Return how many values in the derived sequence are even, including 0 and negative even values. This gives 1.
